access_note: Commercial licence in Pro, Standard and Academic editions; contact Tetcos for pricing and evaluation.
description: NetSim is a commercial packet-level, discrete-event network simulator and emulator. It models 5G and 6G New Radio (massive MIMO, network slicing, non-terrestrial and satellite networks), military tactical radio and MANET, satellite communications in Ku, Ka and X bands, Wi-Fi, IoT and wireless sensor networks, VANET and software-defined networking, and a NetSim Cyber module simulates cyber attacks on power-system and industrial control networks. An emulator connects the simulated network to real hardware running live applications. It is produced by Tetcos, an Indian company whose website reports use by more than 500 organisations in over 30 countries; the current version is 15.0. Coverage: user-built scenarios with no geographic data included; scale is limited by the licence and hardware. Format and access: Windows desktop software with a graphical scenario designer, packet animator, result dashboards and C source for protocol modification; paid, sold in Pro, Standard and Academic editions, with licence prices on request. Caveats: proprietary and Windows-only; model fidelity and scale differ by edition; results are less widely cross-validated than ns-3. Simulation uses: capacity planning of mobile and satellite networks, resilience and cascading-failure studies of communication networks under attack, cyber-physical studies of power grid communications, and network digital twins with the emulator. Related records: ns-3 and OMNeT++ are open alternatives, and Keysight EXata and QualNet are comparable commercial tools.
